claims.statement: The shared model catalog in packages/shared/src/models.ts is the single source of model metadata (id, display name, description, reasoning effort set and default) consumed by the control plane, web UI, and Slack bot; it requires exactly one `default: true` entry or the module throws at load time.

Only OpenAI and xAI (SUBSCRIPTION_PROVIDER_IDS) participate in provider-account routing; each subscription provider has exactly one ModelProviderAccountAdapter (OpenAI and xAI) registered in modelProviderAccountAdapterRegistry, and the registry rejects duplicate adapters at construction.

ModelProviderAccountAdapter is the extension point for a new subscription provider: the provider id must join SUBSCRIPTION_PROVIDER_IDS and the adapter plus a ProviderDeviceAuthorizationCapability must be registered; the broker, selection policy, session snapshot, and sandbox env machinery then follow the shared paths.

Provider credentials are versioned rows ({refreshToken, accessToken?, accessTokenExpiresAt?, accountId?}, schema version 1); every successful refresh or reconnect bumps credential_version, and writes are CAS-guarded on credential version, exchange generation, and exchange owner.

Refresh failures are classified as unauthorized (grant revoked, terminal for the account), ambiguous (network or 5xx, cannot conclude), or retry_safe (transient upstream), and that classification drives whether the credential exchange clears the lease or terminally fences the account to reconnect_required.

Account lifecycle eligibility is centralized in providerAccountIneligibility: active_use operations (runtime access, selection, defaults, verification) require status active and non-archived, while reconnect accepts any non-archived account because it installs a fresh credential and restores active; the service, selection policy, and broker all consult this single function.

Account writes (create, verify, disable/enable, reconnect, archive) and device-authorization finalization are atomic batches through D1ModelProviderAccountAtomicWriter, which composes account, credential, authorization, and first-active-account default statements so a partial failure cannot leave the account row and credential row divergent.

The first active account created for a provider is automatically promoted to the provider default (unattended_mode provider_account) only when no default exists and no other active account exists; disabling or archiving the configured default fails because the default account must remain active.

Device authorization transactions are bounded to a 10-minute lifetime, per-user rate budget of 5 attempts per minute, at most 5 live transactions per user per provider target, and a 1-60 second clamped poll interval; starting a new live transaction supersedes older live ones for the same target, and a stale processing claim (30 s timeout) is failed by the next poll.

Device authorization provider state is persisted only as encrypted payloads (AES-GCM v1) with authenticated data binding the transaction id, provider, and state schema version; the finalizer converges create-on-existing-identity to the existing account (unless disabled) and rejects identity changes during reconnect.

ModelProviderAccountBroker.getAccess validates the account, returns a cached access token when it is more than the 5-minute refresh buffer from expiry, and otherwise runs a single-flight ClaimedProviderCredentialExchange that acquires a durable in_flight lease (bumping exchange_generation), refreshes through the adapter, and rotates credentials only if version, generation, owner, and account status still match.

A stale in-flight credential exchange (owner died past the 15-second exchange timeout) is fenced by a waiter via fenceExchangeAndRequireReconnect, which marks the account reconnect_required and releases the lease in one batch; the fence only commits when the observed lease (version, generation, owner) still matches, so concurrent refresh winners are reconciled instead of being fenced.
Usage attribution (touchLastUsed) is throttled to one write per 15 minutes per account and its failures never invalidate already-persisted authentication state.

Legacy scoped OAuth is a separate credential path: OpenAITokenBroker and XaiTokenRefreshService read and rotate OPENAI_OAUTH_* / XAI_OAUTH_* secrets in their original scope (environment, repo, or global), short-circuit on cached access tokens, and on 401 poll for a concurrently rotated credential before failing; rotated tokens persist back into the original secret scope.

Session provider auth resolution is a strict precedence ladder per subscription provider: explicit api_key, explicit policy-validated account, then the configured default account, with unattended launches forced to api_key when the default's unattendedMode says so, and finally a legacy_scoped_oauth fallback when no default exists; resolution runs once at creation time and the result is pinned immutably in the session.

ProviderAccountSelectionPolicy validates explicit and default selections against the account store and rejects with 400 (invalid id or provider mismatch), 404 (unknown account), or 409 (missing adapter or ineligible account); session-create, automation pin validation, and the settings default endpoint all use it.

The complete provider-auth snapshot (one row per subscription provider) is written in the same D1 batch as the session row; SessionIndexStore.create rejects duplicate or incomplete snapshots, and getCompleteProviderAuth fails closed with 'Session provider auth snapshot is incomplete' when rows are missing, which user-env resolution surfaces so a sandbox never silently loses its pinned routing.

Sessions never re-consult moving provider defaults after creation: changing the default account, disabling, or archiving an account does not move an existing session; agent-spawned children copy the parent's complete snapshot with inheritedFromSessionId and cannot override it.

Automations persist their own provider auth pins; at fire time the scheduler resolves pins with unattended: true, re-labels explicit pins as automation_pin, and records the resolved per-provider rows on every admitted child session, so edits made after the guarded invocation insert cannot change which account an admitted child uses.

prepareManagedProviderEnv strips every control-plane OAuth key from the exposed environment and then per provider: provider_account mode deletes the canonical API key and injects only the non-secret OPENAI_OAUTH_MANAGED / XAI_OAUTH_MANAGED=1 marker; api_key mode retains the canonical API key with no marker; legacy_scoped_oauth emits the marker only when the broker scope (global plus primary repo, excluding secondary repos and environments) actually contains a refresh token, otherwise leaving the API key as fallback.

Image builds predating session routing snapshots use prepareLegacyManagedProviderEnv, which infers legacy_scoped_oauth versus api_key per provider from the build-scope secrets alone; this compatibility path never confers provider_account mode.

getProviderAuthenticationError validates a model's provider against the assembled sandbox environment and the session's pinned modes, requiring the managed marker for provider_account mode, the canonical API key for api_key mode, and either for legacy_scoped_oauth; SessionMessageQueue calls it before dispatching every prompt and fails the message with a user-facing 'No ... authentication is configured' error when unavailable, so unauthenticated provider runs cannot proceed silently.

The sandbox-facing access-token route authenticates the session's sandbox credential and routes by the pinned mode: legacy_scoped_oauth binding proxies the internal legacy refresh handlers, api_key binding returns 409 (the sandbox must use the key it already has), and provider_account binding goes through ModelProviderAccountBroker.getAccess; responses use Cache-Control no-store and carry only short-lived access material.

Provider account and authorization payloads are encrypted with the required 32-byte PROVIDER_ACCOUNTS_ENCRYPTION_KEY using AES-GCM v1, with authenticated additional data binding the account or transaction id, provider, and schema version, so ciphertext cannot be replayed against a different row.

Legacy provider credential locations (global, repository, environment scopes) are inventoried for operators via GET /model-provider-accounts/legacy-credentials, listing every OPENAI_OAUTH_* and XAI_OAUTH_* key; operators remove them only after legacy-bound sessions are gone, and the same rotating refresh token must not be copied into both credential systems.

xAI accounts created before device authorization have no bound external identity and reconnect via one-time refresh token, while every other account reconnects through device authorization; reconnect must authenticate the same provider identity for identity-bound accounts.

Broker access failures map to HTTP statuses at the route boundary: account_not_found to 404, upstream_retry_safe to 502, and all other broker errors (inactive, archived, credential invalid, exchange busy, provider mismatch, reconnect_required) to 409.
